papers.title: Jev-LiteMAS: Separating Decisions from Generation in Multi-Agent Workflows
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems rely on generative models for expert execution, workflow planning, and artifact review. Yet many coordination operations require only bounded decisions, such as selecting the next expert or judging artifact quality. Profiling three representative MAS frameworks, we find that routing and review account for 31.7-43.5% of generative-LLM tokens. However, replacing these operations with low-cost decision models introduces two interface gaps: generative planners produce execution plans and handoff instructions (planning gap), while reviewers provide actionable feedback for repairing flawed artifacts (review gap), which bounded decisions alone cannot provide. We introduce Jev-LiteMAS, a multi-agent framework that bridges both gaps by combining a lightweight decision model (Jev) with generative execution and feedback. To address the planning gap, Jev selects experts dynamically from the task and prior expert outputs, using accumulated context to ground subsequent execution without a pre-generated trajectory. To address the review gap, Jev screens intermediate artifacts against task criteria: passing artifacts proceed directly, whereas flagged ones undergo LLM re-review for acceptance or corrective feedback. Across four benchmarks and two backbones, Jev-LiteMAS reduces generative-LLM tokens by 12.7-54.6% over LAS, maintaining accuracy within 1.34 percentage points and lowering latency in seven of eight settings. Grounding routing in substantive expert outputs prevents up to 18.0 points in accuracy loss.
papers.llm_summary: Jev-LiteMAS tách các thao tác 'ra quyết định' (routing, review) khỏi sinh text trong multi-agent, dùng model nhẹ cho quyết định và chỉ gọi LLM khi cần, giảm 12.7-54.6% token mà giữ accuracy trong 1.34 điểm.
papers.llm_reason: Cực kỳ thực tiễn cho người làm AI: benchmark thật 4 datasets, insight 'dùng model rẻ cho decide, LLM cho generate' áp dụng ngay để cắt cost content pipeline.

papers.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
papers.abstract: Research groups that want a language model grounded in their own literature face a choice between hosted services that receive their unpublished work and self-hosted deployments that keep the data local but give the model no access to the corpus. Munin is an open-source framework for a self-hosted scientific assistant that indexes a group's corpus and its citation graph, and wraps whichever open-weight model the group can serve in an agent harness with specialised reading, search, and computation tools. We claim that the harness, rather than the specific model, is what makes the system useful on domain literature, and we ship the evaluation suite that tests this claim with the software. On 199 paired literature questions, the harness more than doubles the accuracy of the base model, from 0.387 to 0.874 (+0.487, 95% CI [0.407, 0.568]), while naive retrieve-then-answer scores below the unaided model on every backbone tested. Under the harness, roughly twice as many answer claims trace to a passage the model read itself as with fixed top-5 retrieval. When the source paper for a question is removed from the corpus, the system abstains on about nine in ten of the questions it had answered correctly on the Qwen backbones and eight in ten on gpt-oss-20b, and it produces no fabricated local citation across 300 fabricated references. The pattern holds on three backbones from two developers, including a 20-billion-parameter model that runs on a single consumer-grade GPU. With all outbound network access disabled, both Qwen backbones still exceed the published PaperQA2 accuracy. The evaluation suite runs as a single command, so an adopting group can re-run it on its own corpus and model.
papers.llm_summary: MuninAI là framework self-hosted mở để xây trợ lý nghiên cứu trên corpus riêng: harness với tool đọc/tìm/tính toán giúpaccuracy base model tăng hơn 2 lần (0.387→0.874), biết từ chối và không fabricate citation.
papers.llm_reason: Agent harness + tool-use đúng chủ đề cốt lõi, experiment rất chắc (199 câu hỏi, CI, 3 backbone, test chống hallucination), lại cực actionable cho solopreneur làm content research self-hosted; insight 'harness quan trọng hơn model' dùng được ngay.

papers.title: How language model agents reshape price competition
papers.abstract: Repeated Bertrand competition is a stringent benchmark for algorithmic pricing: in homogeneous-goods markets, standard learning procedures typically select the stage-game Nash outcome with prices near marginal cost. We show that LLM pricing agents can escape this benchmark, depending on deployment decisions. LLMs outperform standard online learners through faster adaptation, but this advantage largely disappears against full-information learners. An extracted surrogate algorithm illustrates how LLMs in specific deployments profit from regularly undercutting slower learners. Agents that post one price every period from raw market histories that include rival prices can sustain supracompetitive regimes in self-play. Agents that periodically emit probability distributions from summarized histories of their own profits instead move toward the competitive region in self-play. Markets mixing these interfaces can generate dynamic regimes in which LLMs establish a high-price anchor and regularly undercut it to capture demand. These regimes can keep both competitors' prices above marginal cost. Deployment choices shape these outcomes, shifting the focus from stationary equilibria to dynamic pricing regimes.
papers.llm_summary: Nghiên cứu cách LLM pricing agents thay đổi cạnh tranh giá Bertrand lặp lại, cho thấy lựa chọn giao diện triển khai (đăng giá đơn vs phát phân phối xác suất) quyết định agent có duy trì regime giá trên chi phí biên hay không.
papers.llm_reason: Rất sát business (pricing, cạnh tranh, lợi nhuận) với insight hành động rõ về deployment choices; có benchmark Bertrand và so sánh với online/full-information learners, nhưng experiment thiên về mô phỏng kinh tế.

papers.title: EnterpriseSynth: Zero-Execution SFT and Evaluation Data from OpenAPI Specs
papers.abstract: Tool-using large language model agents require substantial training and evaluation data, yet collecting execution traces from enterprise APIs is often unsafe, expensive, or infeasible because of access controls, compliance constraints, rate limits, and the risk of modifying production data. We present EnterpriseSynth, a zero-execution framework that converts OpenAPI specifications into supervised fine-tuning trajectories and paired evaluation instances without invoking the underlying APIs. The framework uses a four-stage pipeline for specification parsing, intent generation, trajectory synthesis, and static validation. Each generated trajectory is checked against the source specification for endpoint, parameter, type, and schema consistency before being admitted to the dataset. We evaluate EnterpriseSynth on 17 real and synthetic APIs. Adversarial refinement increases the validator's detection rate for planted schema violations from 57-80% to 98% (43/44). Across five random seeds, a compact open-weight model fine-tuned on EnterpriseSynth data outperforms both an untuned model and a Self-Instruct baseline on held-out APIs. Performance remains consistent on five private, hand-authored API specifications that were not available during training, with tool-selection accuracy of 40.0% on the private set and 39.6% on the public held-out set. However, an independent LLM-based evaluation shows that endpoint-selection accuracy substantially overestimates end-to-end correctness: accuracy falls from 48.9% under the endpoint-level metric to 21.3% when argument selection and values are also evaluated. These results demonstrate that OpenAPI specifications can support scalable, execution-free data generation, while highlighting the need for argument-level evaluation when assessing the deployment readiness of tool-using agents.
papers.llm_summary: EnterpriseSynth tạo SFT trajectories và eval data từ OpenAPI specs mà không cần gọi API thật, dùng pipeline 4 giai đoạn + static validation + adversarial refinement.
papers.llm_reason: Rất actionable cho solopreneur muốn build tool-use agent/evaluation data khi không có quyền access API; có benchmark 17 API và metrics rõ ràng.

papers.title: Cost-Efficient Privacy Enforcement for Email-Generating LLM Agents under Strategic Information Requests
papers.abstract: LLM agents now act as delegated communication intermediaries: they read private context, draft messages, and send externally visible emails on behalf of a user. Existing checker-repair defenses can reduce inappropriate disclosure, but they rely on repeated calls to a remote action LLM (the model that drafts and repairs the email) and a remote checker LLM whenever a draft fails validation. This creates a cost problem as well as a privacy problem, especially when a requester strategically asks for exact values, raw records, source evidence, or other details that induce leakage-heavy drafts. We propose local contract-conditioned rewriting as a cost-efficient enforcement layer for email-generating agents. The mechanism intercepts an outgoing draft, constructs an information-release contract that specifies what to preserve, generalize, and forbid, rewrites the draft with a local Gemma rewriter, and selectively invokes a final PrivacyChecker. Across extensive email tasks under normal prompts and attack prompts that operationalize strategic information requests, Gemma + Checker reduces normal-prompt leakage from 11.41% to 4.03% while improving UsableRate (satisfied or partially satisfied outputs) from 85.2% to 92.6%. Under the strategic attack-prompt condition, it reduces leakage from 28.19% to 18.79% and reduces checker-only cost amplification from 1.32x to 1.02x. Offline replay ablation shows that the full contract reduces leakage relative to generic Gemma rewriting by 36.3% under normal prompts and 54.1% under attack prompts. These results support a local-first privacy enforcement design: move repair to a cheaper trusted local layer when possible, but retain the checker as the final semantic gate for high-risk sends.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất lớp thực thi quyền riêng tư cho agent soạn email bằng cách viết lại cục bộ theo hợp đồng thông tin, giảm rò rỉ và tiết kiệm chi phí gọi LLM từ xa.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan agent/tool-use, có experiment thật với số liệu rõ ràng, áp dụng trực tiếp cho automations email/content và tối ưu chi phí cho solopreneur.

papers.title: SAG2: Embedding-Free Multi-Hop Retrieval with BM25 and JEV
papers.abstract: Strong multi-hop retrieval should be practical to deploy without expensive corpus preparation or complex database infrastructure. We present SAG2, an embedding-free retrieval architecture built around a single SQLite database, BM25, and contextual evidence decisions from JEV. SAG2 follows the query-time association principle of SAG (SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation), while replacing its event-entity and dense indexes with a lexical index over original passages. Selected passages supply terms for further retrieval, and newly retrieved evidence guides subsequent decisions. This moves semantic evidence selection to query time, eliminating offline embedding computation, LLM-based event-entity extraction, and dedicated database servers. The resulting system combines lightweight preparation with strong retrieval accuracy: on 1,000-question subsets of MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and HotpotQA, SAG2 achieves the highest Recall@5 and Recall@10 among the compared methods, with Recall@10 of 86.62%, 97.43%, and 99.00%. It also reaches 81.10% document Recall@10 over the 511,962-document EnterpriseRAG-Bench corpus. Indexing all 11,656 MuSiQue passages takes 2.36 seconds, produces a 25.87 MiB database, and requires no model calls. SAG2 demonstrates that accurate multi-hop evidence retrieval can be supported by compact, rapidly prepared infrastructure, making it a practical foundation for knowledge retrieval applications.
papers.llm_summary: SAG2 cho multi-hop retrieval accuracy cao (Recall@10 86.6–99%) chỉ bằng SQLite + BM25, không cần embedding, index 11.656 passage trong 2.36 giây.
papers.llm_reason: RAG thực tiễn, deploy cực nhẹ và benchmark rõ ràng trên 3 dataset + corpus enterprise; rất actionable để tự xây knowledge base/content retrieval rẻ tiền, nhưng thiênên infra hơn business/decision.

papers.title: Designing for Imperfect Prompts: A Simulation-Based Evaluation of an LLM-Based Enterprise Data Assistant Using Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Enterprise data assistants using large language models (LLMs) promise democratized data access in organizations. Yet in our real-world deployment within the CFO unit's data lake at an industry partner, we observed that business users frequently pose imperfect prompts that include domain-specific vocabulary and lack schema references or structural information. This Design Science Research study examines automatic resolution using a semantic mediation layer. We design and evaluate two design variants: schema-based mediation via semantic similarity, and knowledge graph-based mediation leveraging an automatically constructed knowledge graph from the data lake. Our simulation-based evaluation using real-world data, supported by LLM-as-a-Judge assessments and human validation, shows that knowledge graph-based mediation outperforms the schema-based approach in Precision, Recall, F1, and preserving user intent. We propose a design principle for knowledge graph-based mediation, demonstrating that structured knowledge representation bridges user intent and database structure and guides the design of enterprise data assistants across skill levels.
papers.llm_summary: Nghiên cứu triển khai assistant dữ liệu doanh nghiệp cho đơn vị CFO, so sánh mediation bằng schema và bằng knowledge graph tự xây từ data lake với prompt không hoàn hảo.
papers.llm_reason: LLM enterprise assistant + KG, deploy thực tế, LLM-as-Judge và human validation (30+21), insight về bridging user intent–database rất dễ thành content/bài viết cho business (15+14).

papers.title: Asymmetric Dynamic Routing: Balancing Reasoning Depth and Computational Efficiency in Hypergraph RAG
papers.abstract: While graph-based and hypergraph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) significantly mitigate hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs), existing structure-based RAG systems typically adopt static traversal strategies regardless of the query complexity. We identify this ``static retrieval fallacy'' as a primary source of computational redundancy for simple queries and cognitive context gaps for complex reasoning tasks. To balance reasoning quality and inference efficiency, we propose Asymmetric Dynamic Routing (ADR), an intent-conditioned retrieval framework operating over hierarchical knowledge graphs. ADR employs a lightweight structured classifier to dynamically dispatch queries among three asymmetric topological traversal operators: localized fact anchoring, bottom-up adjacency diffusion, and top-down insight grounding, which collectively enable bidirectional information flow across hierarchical knowledge layers. Extensive empirical evaluations across five domain-specific corpora demonstrate that ADR maintains strong reasoning performance while reducing prompt token consumption by up to 48.7\% and end-to-end query latency by 45.3\%, yielding a favorable quality--efficiency trade-off for query-adaptive Hypergraph RAG.
papers.llm_summary: ADR (Asymmetric Dynamic Routing) cho Hypergraph RAG: classifier nhẹ route query vào 3 kiểu traversal tùy độ phức tạp, giảm 48,7% token và 45,3% latency mà giữ chất lượng trên 5 domain.
papers.llm_reason: RAG là công cụ daily của content creator, số liệu giảm cost/latency cực kỳ actionable, insight 'đừng dùng retrieval tĩnh cho mọi query' áp dụng ngay được.

papers.title: Memorilla: Latent Semantic Memory for LLMs
papers.abstract: Memory enables large language models (LLMs) to use information beyond their parameters, such as past user conversations, long documents, or an agent's earlier actions. For a frozen LLM, access to this accumulated knowledge is limited to what a memory system places in its context window. However, gathering and combining relevant information needed for each query while keeping the model's context short remains challenging for existing systems. Here we introduce Memorilla, a memory system that gathers information from an entire document collection into a fixed number of query-dependent 'memory tokens' for a frozen LLM. Memorilla encodes documents (such as user chats, book chapters) once into reusable embeddings, then learns to retrieve and place query-specific information in the LLM's input embedding space. Using only 16 memory tokens, Memorilla achieves the best performance against baselines including Mem0 and MemoRAG on five of eight benchmarks spanning personalization, long-document and knowledge-intensive question answering. Notably, on FactKG, it reaches 84.33% accuracy versus 80.43% with full-context inference, while using 108x fewer tokens to represent the source documents. Furthermore, Memorilla can facilitate continual learning in agentic systems where the document count (the agent's past turns) increases throughout the trajectory. In a TextWorld environment, we show that Memorilla reduces the agent's tendency to wander between rooms it has already explored, and improves its average success rate from 18.6% with full-history in-context learning to 24.2%. Overall, Memorilla aids frozen LLMs in accumulating and using knowledge effectively across long-context interactions and takes a step towards building continually learning AI systems.
papers.llm_summary: Memorilla nén toàn bộ document collection vào 16 'memory tokens' query-dependent cho frozen LLM, đạt 84.33% trên FactKG với 108x ít token hơn full-context.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan LLM memory/personalization, benchmark mạnh (8 benchmarks, thắng Mem0/MemoRAG), insight hành động rõ: cách xây memory system tiết kiệm context cho chatbot/content AI.

papers.title: Can LLMs Fix It Without Code? Toward Automated Verification of No-Code Bug Fixes
papers.abstract: A no-code fix resolves an invalid bug report by directing the user to change a setting, update to a version where the problem is already fixed, or adjust their workflow. Manually verifying whether a proposed no-code fix resolves the reported bug takes considerable developer time. This study proposes an automated, execution-based pipeline for evaluating the capability of large language models (LLMs) to generate no-code fixes in a real browser environment. We evaluate 322 no-code fixes generated by the 12 configurations released with the benchmark of a previous study, covering bug reports categorized as Faulty Configuration, Wrong Version, or External System & Dependency. An executor agent applies each fix by following its natural-language instructions, and an issue-specific checker determines whether the reported bug persists. We repeat the pipeline with three executors: two Computer-Use Agents, OpenCUA-72B and Claude Sonnet 5, and one multimodal agentic LLM, Meta's Muse Glimmer. Only 17.6% of the candidate issues could be set up and passed both sanity gates. Across the 322 fixes, 14.6% to 49.7% resolved the bug depending on the executor, and the strongest configuration, Claude Opus 4.6 in the Vanilla pipeline, resolved up to 74.1% of its fixes under Claude Sonnet 5. Changing only the executor shifted a configuration's resolution rate by 38.8% on average, and the three executors reached the same verdict on only 46.9% of the fixes. Compared with human execution, the executors matched the human consensus for 66.1% to 88.1% of the sampled fixes. Even under the best executor, fewer than half of the LLM-generated no-code fixes resolve the reported bug, so such fixes need verification before they reach users. Execution-based verification can provide this, but the measured capability depends strongly on the executor, which evaluations must report and control.
papers.llm_summary: Nghiên cứu đánh giá LLM/computer-use agent (OpenCUA-72B, Claude Sonnet 5, Muse Glimmer) tạo no-code bug fix trong browser thật, executor agent áp fix theo instruction rồi checker xác minh bug còn không.
papers.llm_reason: Đúng trào lưu computer-use agent đang hot, benchmark 322 fix với số liệu cụ thể (đỉnh 74.1%, đổi executor làm thay đổi 38.8%), insight chọn executor và thiết kế pipeline rất actionable cho content so sánh agent.
